discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can drive a time-reversal-invariant insulator into a new phase, the quantum spin Hall state. They introduced the Z2 topological invariant that separates it from an ordinary insulator. Their work proved that topology classifies band insulators even without a magnetic field, and it led directly to three-dimensional topological insulators with protected Dirac surface states. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells: helical edge channels gave quantized conductance in a non-magnetic material. Together these results created a new class of materials and a worldwide research program. That program spans symmetry-protected and crystalline topological phases, Weyl semimetals, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and routes to topological superconductivity and Majorana modes. Topological band theory now shapes how every electronic material is classified and searched.
